claims.question: q1
claims.claim: Palantir markets its AIP Bootcamp as taking a customer from zero to a working use case in five days.
claims.quote: From 0 to use case in 5 days.

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: Palantir states the five-day AIP Bootcamp is aimed at customers with time-critical missions and has three steps, the first being to understand how to apply AI to mission-critical operations.
claims.quote: 1 / Understand how to apply AI to mission-critical operations

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: The second bootcamp step is developing initial use cases inside the software itself.
claims.quote: 2 / Develop initial use cases in the software

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: The third bootcamp step is onboarding and training users so the use case can be rolled out into operations.
claims.quote: 3 / Onboard and train users for rollout in operations

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: Bootcamp sessions are framed around defining the customer's architecture empirically rather than up front, and moving from chat interfaces to automation.

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: Palantir positions AIP as a way to run LLMs and other AI on a customer's private network securely, which is the platform the bootcamps build on.
claims.quote: Activate LLMs and other AI on your private network, safely and securely.

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: As evidence of results, Palantir cites a news report that its software halved sepsis deaths at a US hospital, with the Sepsis Hub built with Tampa General Hospital in Florida detecting subtle changes in vital signs so antibiotics are given early.
claims.quote: Palantir software halves sepsis deaths at US hospital The Sepsis Hub, developed with Tampa General Hospital in Florida, detects subtle changes in vital signs so antibiotics are given early

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: Palantir's site highlights a CNBC segment in which CEO Alex Karp says something has gone completely wrong with how AI is sold, implying a critique of enterprise AI sales practice.
claims.quote: Palantir CEO Alex Karp says 'something has gone completely wrong' with how AI is sold
